positioning_check: ASIC aggregate as of 21 Sep 2026, a 4-session lag: 218,886,839 shares = 9.63% of 2,271.9m, up from 4.44% on 14 Sep. I pulled the daily series from ASIC's RR files: 100.6m on 15 Sep, 119.5m on 16 Sep (the placement announcement day), 130.5m on 17 Sep, 210.7m on 18 Sep, 218.9m on 21 Sep. The 80m jump on 18 Sep came on 146m shares of volume. That was the index effective date: Vanguard's Form 603 (announced 24 Sep, lodged 23 Sep) shows ~52m bought on 18 Sep at $0.94, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260924/pdf/074fzd3y100thc.pdf. It was also the week before Tranche 1's 203.3m shares at $0.88 settled on 22 Sep and began trading on 23 Sep. The pattern fits placement participants selling short into index demand above the $0.88 issue price and covering by delivery of Tranche 1 stock, not a directional short. On that reading the ~118m increment unwinds without market buying and is not squeeze fuel. That inference is mine, drawn from the timing; I found no document that states it. The 4-session lag means the post-delivery drop, if it happened, is not yet visible. So I discount the baseline's +3.0 short_squeeze component, and I also do not read short_building (−2.0) as bearish conviction. The ~4.4% pre-raise base is long-standing.

outside_window.finding: Tranche 2 (80.8m shares at $0.88, $71.1m) needs shareholder approval at a General Meeting in late October 2026; the SPP closes 19 Oct and its shares begin trading 24 Oct. Project debt finance and FID are targeted for Q1 CY2027. This is the next real funding catalyst, and it is months outside the window.
